description: We aim to build an innovative health monitoring solution that can help astronauts track important health indicators, identify potential health risks, and receive meaningful alerts and insights during long-duration space missions.
summary:
For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I developed ASTRA-VITAL, an innovative, browser-based health-monitoring software concept designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. To address the critical challenge of isolated health tracking, this Minimum Viable Product (MVP) brings key indicators—including heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep patterns, and wellness records—into a unified, highly accessible mission dashboard.

Using HTML and JavaScript logic, the prototype simulates real-time biological data evaluation. It actively processes simulated biometric inputs against established physiological thresholds and instantly triggers automated, color-coded alerts if vitals fall outside nominal parameters. This clear data visualization allows astronauts to easily review changes in their recorded health information, identify readings requiring immediate attention, and maintain a structured medical history.

This solution is important because deep-space missions demand resilient, low-latency monitoring tools that run seamlessly on local devices without relying on delayed backend infrastructure. Operating independently, it empowers crews with autonomous medical oversight. By making complex health information easier to interpret through immediate visual feedback, ASTRA-VITAL helps mission commanders quickly identify anomalies and execute critical interventions, providing a scalable foundation for future space-health monitoring tools.
details:
ASTRA-VITAL: Astronaut Health Assessment and Mission Support System

ASTRA-VITAL is an interactive astronaut health-assessment and mission-support prototype designed to help crew members understand health indicators, explore human body systems and review changes in their health during space missions.

Long-duration spaceflight exposes astronauts to conditions such as microgravity, radiation, isolation and disrupted sleep schedules. These conditions can affect multiple body systems, making regular health assessment and clear interpretation of health indicators important.

How does it work?

ASTRA-VITAL combines an interactive anatomical explorer, crew health assessment, data visualisation and a machine-learning demonstration in one interface.

  • Interactive Anatomy Explorer: Provides selectable male and female anatomical references and views of the normal body, skeleton, muscular system, circulation, nervous system and combined body systems. Clickable anatomical pointers explain the functions of selected structures and relevant spaceflight research context.
  • Crew Health Assessment: Allows users to enter health indicators such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, temperature, sleep duration, fatigue and mood.
  • AI-Assisted Pattern Demonstration: Uses a Random Forest model trained on 18,000 synthetically generated scenarios to demonstrate how combinations of health indicators can be organised into different review categories. Its results are experimental and are not medically validated.
  • Health Trends: Displays recorded observations through interactive charts, allowing users to examine changes over time and compare them with demonstration reference values.
  • Mission Routine: Includes guided educational tasks, daily check-ins and progress tracking to encourage consistent health-recording habits.
  • Research Library and Data Lab: Provides NASA research references and tools for exploring CSV/TSV research datasets, including descriptive statistics and data-completeness checks.

Technology and Development

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with browser-based data storage, interactive visualisations and a 3D anatomy viewer. Python and machine-learning tools were used to generate synthetic training scenarios and develop the Random Forest demonstration model.

NASA's Open Science Data Repository study OSD-575, concerning the Inspiration4 mission, is included as research context. Its pre-flight and post-flight blood-serum biomarker measurements are distinct from continuous wearable sensor readings. The current machine-learning model uses synthetic data rather than claiming to be trained on OSD-575.

Creativity and Intended Impact

ASTRA-VITAL brings anatomical education, health-indicator logging, interactive visualisation and explainable review prompts together in a crew-centred interface. Instead of presenting measurements as isolated numbers, it aims to help astronauts understand what an indicator represents, why it matters and when further review may be appropriate.

The long-term vision is to support astronaut awareness, structured health reporting and communication with flight surgeons during long-duration missions.

Safety and Limitations

ASTRA-VITAL is an educational research prototype, not a validated medical device. It does not diagnose conditions, prescribe treatments or establish astronaut flight-safety thresholds. Any operational use would require validated sensors, clinical validation, qualified flight-medical oversight and mission-specific protocols.

AI assistance was used during concept development, programming and documentation. The AI-generated contributions and external anatomical assets are disclosed separately in the project documentation.
